summary: Ground cabin on a hill above Kings Beach at Lake Tahoe's north end; built in the 1930s (1936 per one compilation); removed in 2002; now a public day-use trail and summit.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 ground cabin; another register photo shows a 20-foot enclosed timber tower
facts.status_note: Lookout removed in 2002; the site remains as a day-use trail and summit with no lookout structure
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

access.note: Day-use, no fee, reached on foot from an iron pipe gate on Lakeshore Avenue (north on Reservoir Drive from Highway 28, then right on Lakeshore Avenue); no camping or overnight stays; park clear of the gate and driveways

visit.trail_note: About half a mile on a paved old forest road (Forest Service Road 1601); 2008 and 2026 sources disagree on the climb (about 100 ft vs 335-400 ft)

events.note: Compilation says 'A lookout cabin constructed' in 1936; the register gives only the 1930s

August 1937: Lookout Fireman Johnny Nelson on Stateline Point took in a fawn a tourist had accidentally hit on the highway; the fawn, later named Duke, spent the winter at the Galena Creek ERA camp, where workers decided it should be chief mascot (reported in a November 18, 1938 newspaper item)
Forest fire near Kings Beach put out by lookout J. E. Cox and Forest Patrolman C. R. Arment; believed started by a thrown cigarette
Harold (Doc) Thornton received a $150 award for superior performance; the compilation says he served the North Shore tower at Crystal Bay for two summers
Registered April 10, 2020 as FFLOS US 1987, CA 115
Nine new interpretive panels installed along the trail, replacing older weather-worn signs

corrections.why: The register's Built field reads 1930's, not 1930; the compilation dates a lookout cabin to 1936
Two sources describe the site as a day-use visit with no fee; no source describes a closure or permit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 1930's; compilation says a cabin was constructed in 1936. Story reports both and does not pick one.
A 2008 newspaper walk gives about 100 feet of elevation gain; a 2026 guide gives 335-400 feet. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: Build year: register says 1930's, compilation says 1936; the brief's 1930 is not in the register (see corrections). The 1936 year comes from a compilation of newspaper items, so it is secondary. Staffing and 1940 fire items are secondhand newspaper quotes on the compilation page; the 1964 Crystal Bay tower is linked to Stateline only by that compilation. Access is upgraded from unknown to public based on 2026 and resort listings; the Forest Service recreation page fetched did not give readable detail on this site. Climb sources disagree (about 100 ft vs 335-400 ft). The Marin 2008 walk and the 2026 guide are the only sources describing the site today. Worth a human check: current Forest Service signage or rules for the gate and parking.
